note: scripts/hook_guard.py — the mutation guard's sibling for the hooks. Each gate has a unit test; this proves the next thing up, that the WIRING holds: a forbidden event fed through the real hooks/nestor-hook comes back a deny in the spelling the harness honors, and a benign one comes back allow. Idea from hook-gym (MIT); clean-room.

decisions.question: The gates have unit tests. What does a separate harness add?
decisions.commitment: It drives every gate end-to-end through the real nestor-hook wrapper (not the pure evaluator) and asserts the block lands on the wire, plus a coverage pin: the blocking-gate set is derived from hook_runner.MODULES minus the context-only modules, and a gate with no deny case fails the run. tests/test_hook_guard.py asserts it passes live, that the pin has no gap, that removing before_bash's case reopens a gap, and that a mislabeled case is reported wrong.
decisions.why: A unit test proves the evaluator denies; it does not prove the runner dispatches to it or that the deny is spelled the way Claude Code reads. That wiring is exactly what silently rots — a gate wired to the wrong module name, or emitting a spelling PreToolUse ignores, degrades to advice while every unit test stays green. The pin is willow-mcp's lesson: mcp_federation once shipped in the gate with no guard behind it. A gate that cannot be shown to deny on the wire has not been shown to work.
